title: View transitions
summary: Page-owned transitions into and out of routes, without a router-selected animation.

sections.title: Export presentation from the destination
sections.body: Export viewTransition(commit, previous, next) from a page route module. A destination page export wins; otherwise the nearest nested layout export applies. Both React and Preact support the same contract. Flat applications use mountApplication; nested routing is client-only. Without an export, the router commits normally. This replaces the previous NavigateOptions.viewTransition boolean, including the option in stable 0.4.11. Move that behavior into the route export.

sections.title: The consumer owns the browser transition
sections.body: Your presentRoute function decides whether to call commit immediately or pass it to document.startViewTransition. Check browser support and reduced-motion preference yourself. Initial loading, errors and same-URL updates can also reach the callback, so choose which updates should animate. The return value is not awaited. Call commit to complete presentation; stale and repeated calls are ignored. Handle the browser transition promises and errors in your application. Smolter supplies no animation defaults or automatic full-document fade.

sections.title: Leave the document from the current page
sections.body: When navigation leaves the document — a configured document handoff, a cross-origin router.navigate, or a Link to another application — Smolter calls the current page's viewTransition, falling back to its nearest nested layout. next.leaving is true, next.url is the destination and next.path is absent. Calling commit performs the departure through leaveDocument, or location.assign without one, once. Animate the outgoing page first, then call commit. Pages without an export leave immediately, so departures stay per-page rather than global. Ordinary external anchors that are not handoffs keep browser handling. The destination document presents its own entry: its first commit reaches viewTransition with previous.loaded false.

sections.title: Move a shared image
sections.body: Give corresponding old/new images the same unique view-transition-name. Pass commit to the browser transition API so the old capture precedes the route change and the new capture follows it. Prepare destination images and reserve dimensions when necessary. A shared name cannot identify multiple rendered elements in the same state. Remote image loading and browser support still affect the result.

sections.title: Unused support and cleanup
sections.body: The Vite plugin removes transition dispatch for statically analyzed file-route applications that do not use viewTransition. Manual route factories, opaque references, namespace imports and computed writes retain support conservatively. HMR rechecks capability usage. Separate nested entrypoints keep layout code out of flat applications. Imperative page animation controllers that must stop before the next paint should use layout-effect cleanup; a passive effect may clean up after navigation has already reset scrolling.
